subject: How to run CFA or SEM in LAVAAN when Indicator Variables for measuring the Latent Variables are binary categorical

messages.author: 1976ee0368c51a69
messages.subject: How to run CFA or SEM in LAVAAN when Indicator Variables for measuring the Latent Variables are binary categorical
parts:
Dear LAVAAN community

I am struggling with the following issue. 
For the measurement of the latent variables, the indicators variables that I am using are all binary categorical variables having two levels (0 for no, and 1 for yes).
For instance, for measuring X =~ x1+ x2+ x3 (all the xi take either of the two values: 0/1). And as per my understanding, the default measure in LAVAAN is MLE which is for continuous indicator variables. So when I run the SEM command, I am getting different warning messages and the model is not running accurately.
I looked at various places and there are suggestions like keeping the value of categorical indicator variables in numeric terms (like 1,2,3) will work but apparently it is not. further I checked that the degrees of freedom are positive so there should not be a problem of identification which might be generating warning messages.

Can anyone please take out some time and help me out in this. I have been struggling and have spent a lot of time but could not find a solution. The examples and explanations given everywhere is either about continuous variables or about the ordered argument in the SEM function (which is also not working for me).

Regards
Priya

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: How to run CFA or SEM in LAVAAN when Indicator Variables for measuring the Latent Variables are binary categorical
parts:
Priya,

Positive degrees of freedom means you don't have a certain type of identification problem, but a model can also be locally unidentified. One of the places this often happens is a factor with rare categorical indicators.

It's hard to help more without more information. What is your model? If your model is large, please post a small version that still causes the problem. What is your sem() call? What is the exact language of the warnings you are getting? Are they warnings or errors? Warnings don't necessarily invalidate your results, though you should certainly consider them and why you're getting them.

Pat

messages.subject: Re: How to run CFA or SEM in LAVAAN when Indicator Variables for measuring the Latent Variables are binary categorical
parts:
Priya,

Thanks for the additional information.

Let's start with the first error:

missing observed variables in dataset: f_tv f_smart_phone f_computer f_open_read_sms  f_mobile_banking
 f_online_phone_apps

It tells you what the problem is. These newly created variables aren't in the dataframe eth.

Instead of:
f_tv <- factor(tv, levels = c("0", "1"), ordered = TRUE)

try

eth$f_tv <- factor(eth$tv, levels = c("0", "1"), ordered = TRUE)

That will put the new variable into eth so it will be available to cfa().

Also, one of your attempts resulted in:

WARNING: ordered variable(s): ICT_access ICT_capability
  could not be found in the data and will be ignored

ICT_access and ICT_capability aren't in the eth dataset because they're latent variables you're estimating from the observed variables. (Also, even with ordered indicators, the latents aren't ordered, butthat's a different issue.)

Hope that helps.

Pat
